releases.title: One personality, weekly check-in, easier installs, first ten minutes, host a friend

items.text: How Sara comes across (Settings → Sara → Name and personality): one personality for chat, her voice, email drafts and your website receptionist.
Her weekly check-in shows what she did, what failed and what cost money, with three ideas you can accept in one tap.
The first ten minutes: Set up Sara looks at this computer and offers the right way to run her model, then ends with three quick wins.
Host a Sara for a friend (Settings → Household → People on this server).
Every installer checks the machine before it changes anything: disk space, memory, the port, the system and its version, a 64-bit CPU, an earlier install.
When another program already uses her port, Sara now says so with the next step instead of stopping with a long error.

releases.title: What Sara knows, polite nudges, continue on another device, Mac parity

items.text: One "What I know about you" page. Settings → You → What Sara knows now lists everything she knows about you by topic, with where and when she learned it and how long ago.
Her nudges share one polite daily budget, most useful first, with the rest in an evening roundup.
Continue on another device. Your open chat, the words you hadn't sent, where you were reading and an open Talk or live view follow you.
The screen companion on the Mac. Offer help when an error shows on screen now works in the Mac app too, with the same rules and bubble as on Windows.
Tell Sara a renewal date in a chat ("my passport expires March 31, 2027, keep track of it") and it goes on You → Renewals with its reminder.
The benchmark page shows the everyday real-model task runs task by task; the real-model suite has 13 more tasks, one per newer feature.

releases.title: She knows the time, Always allow, six languages everywhere

items.text: Words as you speak in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and Italian.
Always allow everything (Settings → Connections → Computer use).
The email bridge no longer sends the same reply twice.
A command she runs on your computer that goes past its time limit is now always stopped.
Sara now knows exactly when everything was said, so she no longer says "yesterday" about something from 10 minutes ago.

releases.title: She knows what she did, second opinion from chat, sharper memory

items.text: The Action timeline also lists changes she makes without asking first (a live checklist she posts, for example), using the same rule as the claim checker.
Her memory picks and auto-loaded skills no longer match on everyday words.
"She said it, did it happen?" no longer shows on things she really did with her newer tools.

releases.title: Offline answers on the phone, teach by showing, Wear OS, live views, second opinion

items.text: Second opinion on any of her replies (the ⋯ actions under a reply → Get a second opinion): two other connected models answer your question on their own.
Live views in chat: she can post a small checklist you tick, a table or a bar or line chart right in the chat, and it keeps itself up to date from where its data lives.
Sara on a Wear OS watch: a tile with the rest of today's reminders, how many things wait on you and a Talk button that asks her by voice and shows her short answer.
Answers while offline (Android app; Settings → Connections → Devices and sign-in → Offline on this device): an optional small model on the phone.
Teach by showing (browser extension → Watch me do this): do a task once in your browser and Sara keeps the steps (clicks, what you typed, what you picked, the pages).

releases.title: Photo search, interpreter, health imports, captions, action timeline, privacy ledger, legacy access

items.text: What left this server (Settings → Privacy & system → Privacy): a day-by-day list of every request her server sent to another computer, grouped by why it went.
Caregiver mode (Health → Daily check-in, Caregivers, Simple home): a person can let an adult in their household see their missed doses, their daily check-ins, or both.
Accessibility switch (Settings → You → Appearance → Accessibility, also a quick setting on the Settings home): one switch for easier reading.
Action timeline (Settings → Privacy & system → Reports → Action timeline): one list of what she changed for you, newest first, for 90 days: files.
Legacy and emergency access (Settings → Privacy & system → Privacy): name one person you trust and pick what they get.
Live and translated captions for meetings (Library → Meetings → a meeting → Captions): big captions that follow a room or a recording while she hears it.

releases.title: My apps, automation replay, workforce report, Fix this issue, website receptionist

items.text: Automation steps and replay (Settings → You → Automations): Steps opens an automation's step list.
Workforce report and one-click hire: once a week.
Fix this issue (Settings → Connections → Apps and services → GitHub → Fix an issue): a repository's open issues, each with one button.
My apps (Library → My apps): ask her for a small web app in a chat, try it and say "keep it".
Website receptionist (Settings → You → Business details → Website receptionist): a chat for your own website, added with one line of code.

releases.title: Renewals, purchases, Home Assistant scenes, audio briefing, scan pages, upkeep, gifts

items.text: Car and house upkeep (Settings → You → My details → Car and house upkeep): add the usual schedule for a car.
Gifts and occasions: each People card now shows the next birthday and yearly dates, a gift budget, gift ideas from what she knows.
One-minute voice journal: Library → Journal. Pick how today was, press Record a minute and talk (or type it), and the entry is saved with its mood.
Find a time with a friend: in a one-to-one Messages chat (or by asking her, "find a time with Sam for coffee").
Snap and file: Library → Scan pages takes pages with the phone or computer camera (or photos you already have), finds the paper's edges.
Morning briefing as audio (Settings → You → Briefing and reminders → Listen to your briefing).
